correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed from the complete-multipartite distance structure. Ordinary general-position sets are exactly subsets of one part or sets meeting every part at most once. Mutual maximal distance was checked pairwise: same-part pairs always qualify, while cross-part pairs qualify exactly when both endpoint parts are singletons. Simplicial vertices were characterized directly from their neighborhoods. Convex complements were characterized by the exact interval identity for a same-part pair. Combining these facts yields the dual-set dichotomy and all polynomial cases. Edge cases including complete graphs, stars, \(K_{2,1}\), \(K_{2,2}\), \(K_{3,2}\), and mixtures of singleton and non-singleton parts agree with the formulas. The standalone exhaustive certificate checks all 8084 subsets across all 58 multipartite types through order eight, with 32336 property comparisons and 174 polynomial comparisons.

originality.rationale: The source paper introducing the three variants, the checked later survey material, exact phrase searches, parameter-synonym searches, and semantic searches did not locate a complete-multipartite dual classification or the displayed dual enumerator. The accumulated local findings were also checked for dual/outer/total general-position terminology and equivalent claims, with no overlap. The claim is deliberately narrowed: the source characterizations are credited, ordinary complete-multipartite general position is not claimed new, and possible implicit prior coverage of the outer-number consequence through strong-resolving-graph theory is excluded from the novelty claim.

value.rationale: Dual general position is non-hereditary and can have value zero, so a complete structural classification is not a routine substitution into a monotone parameter. The result identifies an exact phase transition for a canonical graph family, including an infinite family with only the empty dual set, and upgrades the numerical parameter to a full counting polynomial. Companion outer and total enumerators place all three variants on the same complete-multipartite family for direct comparison.
